author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Merge two PS2 library folders with a hash-led conflict table
summary: Consolidate two playable roots into a fresh destination by classifying identical hashes, regional revisions, multidisc sets, and patched working copies before EmuCoreX ever scans the merged folder.
heroAlt: Media Preservation Frontend showing optical-media identity fields used to distinguish source discs during a merge

blocks.text: Merge into a third folder, never into either source

A safe merge preserves Folder A and Folder B while building an empty Folder C. That third location makes every decision reversible. Filename collision is only the first signal: identical hashes can use different names, while matching names can hide different regions, revisions, discs, or externally patched working copies. The conflict table must therefore store path, bytes, SHA-256, serial, region, and role in a multidisc set.

Do not let a file manager answer Replace, Skip, or Keep both for the whole operation. Those buttons do not know which copy is a verified master, which is patched, or whether Disc 2 belongs beside Disc 1.
Build inventories for A and B

items: Read-only SHA-256 reports for both source roots.
Enough separate capacity for the complete deduplicated destination.
Dump logs or serial records for ambiguous regional and revision pairs.
A naming convention that includes disc number where required.
Both source roots temporarily removed from EmuCoreX scanning during final acceptance.
1. Join the two inventories by hash to identify byte-identical files regardless of name.
2. Join again by normalized filename to expose same-name, different-hash conflicts.
3. For identical hashes, choose one canonical working filename and record which source supplied it.
4. For different hashes, inspect serial, region, revision, disc number, and patch status; keep each legitimate variant under an unambiguous name.
5. Copy classified files into empty Folder C in groups, then calculate a fresh destination hash report.
6. Compare C with the conflict table and verify that every planned variant and multidisc component exists once.
7. Authorize only Folder C in EmuCoreX, refresh, and test one entry from every conflict class.
8. Retain A and B read-only until C survives restart and each regional or multidisc identity is correct.

blocks.text: A patched image should not replace an untouched preservation master. Prefer external patching where supported and keep the master outside active scans. If a cue file references tracks, the entire set receives one conflict decision; copying only the cue or the largest BIN creates a misleading but incomplete library item.
Close every row in the conflict table
A merge is complete when each input file has a documented disposition and each output has an integrity record.

items: Every identical-hash group contributes one intended active copy.
Different-hash collisions have explicit serial, region, revision, or patch explanations.
Every multidisc and cue/bin set is complete.
Destination hashes match the selected input copies.
EmuCoreX shows the planned titles without overlapping source roots.
Two files share a title but lack serial evidence: preserve both outside the active root until identified.
Destination hash matches neither source: repeat the copy from the chosen verified file.
A cue boots without audio: one referenced track was renamed or omitted.
Favorites attach to the wrong region: correct image identity before moving saves or profiles.

blocks.text: Discard C and return to the source map

Remove Folder C's grant, refresh, and re-authorize A and B exactly as they were. Because neither source was modified, no reverse copy is needed. Preserve the conflict table, mark the disputed rows, and rebuild C only after those identities are resolved.
Deduplication and backup retention are different decisions

One active copy per hash prevents library clutter, but a second offline copy on another physical device is legitimate resilience. The hash table should distinguish Active, Preservation master, and Backup so a cleanup never removes the final recoverable copy.
